source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Use equal patient counts as the main rule even when acuity and required nursing care differ substantially.","B":"Match client acuity and care needs with nurse competence, workload, and available resources rather than relying on numbers alone.","C":"Give the most complex clients to the least experienced nurse so difficult assignments are distributed evenly.","D":"Base assignments mainly on room location because geographic efficiency outweighs differences in acuity."}}
source_row.rationale: The current NCSBN test plan directs nurses to prioritize care based on acuity and to make assignments/delegations according to client needs and personnel competency while considering available resources. Equal numbers alone do not establish a safe workload.
source_row.source_detail: Management of Care — prioritization by acuity and ‘Assignment, Delegation and Supervision’ based on client needs/personnel competency; recognition of available resources. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care; Assignment, Delegation and Supervision; prioritization/continuity/client rights as applicable. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
source_row.stem: A charge nurse assigns one RN a client needing frequent complex wound care, another with unstable hemodynamics, and two stable clients. Which principle should guide the assignment?
